title: To do or doing?
goal: Know which verbs take “to + verb” and which take “-ing”
intro: When one verb follows another, the second verb is either “to + verb” (I want to go) or “-ing” (I enjoy going). It depends on the first verb, so it has to be learned. Also, after a preposition (in, of, about, for, to in “look forward to”), always use -ing.

rules.rule: + to do: want, need, decide, hope, plan, promise, agree, learn, manage, would like.
+ doing: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest, keep, practise, consider, can’t help.

examples: I’m looking forward to meeting you.

mistakes.wrong: I look forward to meet you.
mistakes.right: I look forward to meeting you.

mistakes.wrong: I am used to wake up early.
mistakes.right: I am used to waking up early.

ex.q: I am looking forward to hear from you.
ex.fixed: I am looking forward to hearing from you.

ex.a: I'm looking forward to seeing you soon.

ex.q: Correct this: “I look forward to work with you.”
a: I look forward to working with you
I am looking forward to working with you

talk: Talk about what you enjoy doing, what you want to do this year, and what you’re looking forward to. Use at least three -ing and three “to” forms.
